entry_json.definition: the money you are paid for your job, usually the same amount every month
entry_json.own_context_sentence: In my country a teacher's salary is lower than most people expect.
example_sentences: She took the job even though the salary was quite low.
Salaries in the city are higher, but so is the rent.

confusables.difference: A salary is fixed and usually paid monthly to office or professional staff. A wage is usually paid weekly or by the hour for manual or shift work.

entry_json.definition: the act of selling something; also a time when a shop sells things more cheaply
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I bought this coat in the January sale for half price.
example_sentences: Car sales fell sharply during the crisis.
The house has been up for sale since March.

confusables.difference: Sale is the noun and sell is the verb. You sell a car; the sale of the car took a month. Never "I saled it".

entry_json.definition: the white powder you add to food to make it taste better
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Doctors say most of us eat far too much salt without noticing.
example_sentences: Could you pass the salt, please?
Reducing salt in processed food would improve public health.

entry_json.definition: not different; exactly like something else
entry_json.own_context_sentence: My brother and I went to the same school for eleven years.
example_sentences: We take the same bus every morning.
The results were almost the same in both groups.
entry_json.avoid: Always use "the" before same: "the same day", never "a same day".

entry_json.definition: two pieces of bread with food between them
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I usually make a sandwich at home rather than buy lunch.
example_sentences: She had a cheese sandwich and a coffee at her desk.
The café does very good chicken sandwiches.

entry_json.definition: a thick wet food that you put on or with other food to give it more taste
entry_json.own_context_sentence: My mother makes a tomato sauce that takes three hours.
example_sentences: The fish came with a lemon sauce.
Add the sauce at the end so it does not burn.

entry_json.definition: to keep money to use later; also to stop someone from dying or being hurt
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I am saving about a fifth of my income for a deposit on a flat.
example_sentences: Cycling to work saves me nearly forty pounds a month.
The doctors saved his life.

confusables.difference: You save money by not using it; you spend money by using it. Learners sometimes say "save time on my phone" when they mean spend.

entry_json.definition: to speak words
entry_json.own_context_sentence: She said that the course was harder than she expected.
example_sentences: He said nothing for a long time.
What did the teacher say about the deadline?

confusables.difference: You say something, but you tell somebody something. "He told me the news" is right; "He said me the news" is wrong. Use "say to me" if you want a person after say.

entry_json.avoid: Do not put a person straight after say. Say to me, or tell me, but never "say me".

entry_json.definition: feeling afraid
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I was scared of speaking English in public until my second year.
example_sentences: She is scared of flying, so she takes the train.
There is no reason to be scared of the examiner.

confusables.difference: Scared describes the person who feels the fear; scary describes the thing that causes it. "I was scared because the film was scary." Saying "I am scary" means you frighten other people.

entry_json.definition: making you feel afraid
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Giving a talk in front of forty people was scary the first time.
example_sentences: The road up the mountain is quite scary at night.
It sounds scary, but the test is easier than people say.
entry_json.avoid: Scary is informal. In Task 2 writing prefer frightening or worrying.

entry_json.definition: a part of a film, play or book; also a view of a place
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The opening scene of the film is set in a busy market.
example_sentences: My favourite scene is the one at the station.
Police arrived at the scene within minutes.

confusables.difference: A scene is one part of a story or one particular place. Scenery is the natural landscape you look at, and it is uncountable: "beautiful scenery", never "beautiful sceneries".

entry_json.definition: a plan that lists when things will happen
entry_json.own_context_sentence: My study schedule puts speaking practice on Tuesday and Thursday.
example_sentences: The building work is two months behind schedule.
I keep a weekly schedule so nothing gets forgotten.

entry_json.definition: a place where children go to learn
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I went to a state school about ten minutes from my house.
example_sentences: She left school at sixteen and started working.
Children in my country start school at the age of six.
entry_json.avoid: When you mean attending as a student, say "go to school" with no article. "Go to the school" means going to the building, for example as a parent.

entry_json.definition: the study of the physical world through tests and careful watching
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Science was my strongest subject at secondary school.
example_sentences: She wants to study science at university.
Government funding for science has been cut.

entry_json.definition: a person who works in science
entry_json.own_context_sentence: A scientist at our university is testing a cheaper water filter.
example_sentences: Scientists have warned about this for thirty years.
He trained as a scientist before moving into teaching.

entry_json.definition: the number of points or marks someone gets in a test or game
entry_json.own_context_sentence: My score in the practice test went up by half a band.
example_sentences: The final score was two goals to one.
A score of six is enough for most courses.

entry_json.definition: the flat part of a television, phone or computer where you see pictures
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I try to keep my screen time under two hours a day.
example_sentences: Children spend too many hours in front of a screen.
The text was too small to read on such a little screen.

entry_json.definition: the large area of salt water that covers much of the earth
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I grew up two streets from the sea, so I swam every summer.
example_sentences: The sea was too cold for swimming in April.
Sea levels are rising faster than expected.

confusables.difference: The sea is the general word and often means water near the coast. An ocean is one of the five huge named bodies of water, such as the Pacific Ocean.

entry_json.definition: to look carefully for something
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I searched for a cheap flight for nearly an hour.
example_sentences: Rescue teams searched the area all night.
She searched online for a course near her home.
entry_json.avoid: Search for something when you are looking for it. "Search something" means to examine that place or person, as police search a bag.

entry_json.definition: one of the four parts of the year; also the time of year when something happens
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Spring is the season I like most because the weather is mild.
example_sentences: Hotels are much more expensive in the tourist season.
Which season do you prefer, summer or winter?

entry_json.definition: something you sit on, for example in a bus, cinema or car
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I always try to get a window seat on long flights.
example_sentences: There were no seats left on the last train.
Please take a seat; the doctor will call you.

entry_json.definition: used to introduce the second point in a list of reasons
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Firstly, the fees are high; secondly, the course is very long.
example_sentences: Secondly, public transport would reduce traffic in the centre.
Firstly it saves money, and secondly it saves time.
entry_json.avoid: If you start with "secondly", you must have started the earlier point with "firstly" or "first". Do not use it alone.

entry_json.definition: something you do not tell other people
entry_json.own_context_sentence: She kept the news a secret until the results came out.
example_sentences: Can you keep a secret?
The secret of his success was simply hard work.

entry_json.definition: a person in an office who types letters, answers calls and keeps records
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The department secretary sent me the form the same afternoon.
example_sentences: Ask the secretary to book the meeting room.
She worked as a secretary before retraining as an accountant.

entry_json.definition: one part of something larger
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The reading test has three sections and one hour in total.
example_sentences: Please complete section B of the form.
The last section of the report lists the main findings.

entry_json.definition: to notice something with your eyes; also to understand
entry_json.own_context_sentence: From my window I can see the whole park.
example_sentences: I saw her at the station yesterday.
I see what you mean now.

confusables.difference: See happens without effort; look at is something you choose to do. "I looked at the chart and saw a clear rise." Also, see is not normally used in the continuous: say "I can see it", not "I am seeing it".

entry_json.definition: to appear to be a certain way
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The course seems difficult at first, but the structure is clear.
example_sentences: He seems tired this week.
It seems that prices will keep rising.
entry_json.avoid: Seem is not used in the continuous. Say "she seems happy", never "she is seeming happy".

entry_json.definition: to give something to someone who pays you money for it
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I sold my old laptop and put the money towards a new one.
example_sentences: The shop sells fresh bread every morning.
They had to sell the house after he lost his job.

confusables.difference: The seller gives the goods and takes the money; the buyer takes the goods and gives the money. "I sold it to her" and "she bought it from me" describe the same event.

entry_json.definition: to make something go to another person or place
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I sent the application on Monday and heard back on Friday.
example_sentences: Could you send me the file by tonight?
The company sends staff abroad for training.

entry_json.definition: the ability to understand or feel something; a good reason for doing something
entry_json.own_context_sentence: It makes sense to book the test once you are ready.
example_sentences: She has a very good sense of humour.
There is no sense in paying twice for the same thing.

entry_json.definition: a group of words that makes a complete idea in writing or speech
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I try to keep each sentence short so my meaning is clear.
example_sentences: Read the sentence again and find the mistake.
A paragraph usually opens with a topic sentence.

entry_json.definition: not joined to something else; different and on its own
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The kitchen and the living room are separate in my flat.
example_sentences: Please write your answers on a separate sheet.
They have separate accounts for saving and spending.
entry_json.avoid: Watch the spelling: sep-a-rate, with an a in the middle, not "seperate". As a verb it is pronounced ˈsepəreɪt.

entry_json.definition: a number of similar things that come one after another; a set of television programmes
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The college ran a series of free workshops on writing.
example_sentences: There has been a series of accidents on that road.
I watched the whole series in a weekend.
entry_json.avoid: Series is the same in singular and plural. There is no word "serie".

entry_json.definition: very bad or dangerous; or not joking
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Air pollution is a serious problem in most large cities.
example_sentences: She suffered a serious injury and missed the season.
Are you serious about moving abroad?

entry_json.definition: to give food or drink to someone; to do work that helps people
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The café serves breakfast until eleven.
example_sentences: He served in the army for six years.
Dinner is served at seven in the hotel.

entry_json.definition: work that a person or organisation does for the public
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The bus service to my village runs only twice a day.
example_sentences: Customer service at that bank is very slow.
Health services are free at the point of use.

entry_json.definition: to move quickly from side to side or up and down
entry_json.own_context_sentence: My hands were shaking before the speaking test.
example_sentences: Shake the bottle before you open it.
We shook hands and the interview began.

entry_json.definition: the form of something on the outside, for example round or square
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The new library has an unusual shape, almost like a wave.
example_sentences: Cut the paper into the shape of a circle.
Regular exercise keeps you in good shape.

entry_json.definition: to have or use something together with other people
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I share a flat with two other students to keep the rent down.
example_sentences: Would you like to share a taxi?
She shared her notes with the whole class.

entry_json.definition: the word used for a woman or girl you have already mentioned
entry_json.own_context_sentence: My sister is a nurse, and she works nights most weeks.
example_sentences: She told me the class had been moved.
She has lived in Manchester since 2019.

entry_json.definition: a farm animal kept for its meat and for its soft hair, which is used to make warm clothes
entry_json.own_context_sentence: There are more sheep than people in the hills where my grandparents live.
example_sentences: The farmer keeps about two hundred sheep.
Sheep were grazing on the hillside above the village.
entry_json.avoid: The plural of sheep is sheep. Never write "sheeps".

entry_json.definition: a thin flat piece of something, especially paper; also the large piece of material you put on a bed
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Write your answers on a separate sheet of paper.
example_sentences: I changed the sheets on the bed this morning.
The teacher handed out a sheet with the key vocabulary.

entry_json.definition: a large boat that carries people or goods on the sea
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Most of what we buy arrives by ship rather than by plane.
example_sentences: The ship left the port at dawn.
Container ships burn a great deal of fuel.

confusables.difference: A ship is large and crosses seas; a boat is smaller and usually stays on rivers, lakes or near the coast.

entry_json.definition: a piece of clothing for the top of your body, with a collar and buttons
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I wear a shirt for interviews and a T-shirt everywhere else.
example_sentences: He ironed a clean shirt for the meeting.
The shirt was too tight around the neck.

entry_json.definition: a thing you wear on your foot
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I need a new pair of shoes for walking to work.
example_sentences: Take your shoes off before you come in.
These shoes are comfortable but they were expensive.
entry_json.avoid: Shoes come in pairs, so say "a pair of shoes" rather than "a shoe" when you mean both.

entry_json.definition: a building where you buy things
entry_json.own_context_sentence: There is a small shop at the end of my street that opens late.
example_sentences: The shop closes at six on Sundays.
Online shopping has forced many local shops to close.

confusables.difference: Shop is the usual British word; store is the usual American one. In British English a store is normally large, as in department store.

entry_json.definition: the activity of buying things in shops
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I do the shopping online because it saves me an hour every week.
example_sentences: We went shopping for winter clothes.
Shopping centres have changed the way town centres look.
entry_json.avoid: Say "go shopping" for the activity and "do the shopping" for buying food you need.

entry_json.definition: not long in size or time; not tall
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The course is short, just six weeks, but very intensive.
example_sentences: It is only a short walk from the station.
She is short, so she sits near the front.

entry_json.definition: the part of your body between your neck and your arm
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I carry my bag on one shoulder and it gives me back pain.
example_sentences: He hurt his shoulder playing tennis.
She looked over her shoulder to check the road.

entry_json.definition: to say something very loudly
entry_json.own_context_sentence: There is no need to shout; I can hear you.
example_sentences: Someone shouted from the other side of the street.
The coach shouted instructions to the players.

confusables.difference: Shout at somebody means you are angry with them. Shout to somebody just means you are far away and want to be heard.

entry_json.definition: to let someone see something; to make something clear
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The graph shows a steady rise in energy use since 2010.
example_sentences: Could you show me how the machine works?
She showed me her photographs from the trip.

entry_json.definition: a thing that sends water down so you can wash your whole body
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I have a shower every morning before I leave for work.
example_sentences: The shower in the hotel had no hot water.
There were a few showers of rain in the afternoon.

entry_json.definition: to close something
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Please shut the window; it is getting cold.
example_sentences: The library shuts at nine on weekdays.
He shut the door quietly behind him.

confusables.difference: Shut and close mean the same for doors and windows, but shut is more informal. In writing, and for roads or businesses, prefer close.

entry_json.definition: not well; ill
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I was sick for a week and missed two lessons.
example_sentences: She had to take three days off sick.
Feeling sick on the bus is common for me.

confusables.difference: In British English, "be sick" often means to vomit, while "be ill" means to have a health problem. Americans use sick for both.

entry_json.definition: one of the two or more flat parts on the outside of something; a position next to something
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The shops are all on the other side of the road.
example_sentences: Write on one side of the paper only.
Both sides of the argument have some strength.

entry_json.definition: a board with words or a picture that gives information
entry_json.own_context_sentence: A sign at the entrance said the pool was closed for cleaning.
example_sentences: Follow the signs to the exit.
Rising sea levels are a clear sign of a warming planet.

entry_json.definition: an expensive bright grey-white metal, used for cups, medals and jewellery
entry_json.own_context_sentence: She wore a thin silver chain her grandmother gave her.
example_sentences: The cup is made of silver.
He won a silver medal at the national championships.

entry_json.definition: almost the same, but not exactly
entry_json.own_context_sentence: My results were similar to the ones I got last month.
example_sentences: The two cities are similar in size.
We had similar problems with the old system.

confusables.difference: Similar means nearly alike; same means with no difference at all. Also the grammar differs: similar to something, but the same as something.

entry_json.avoid: Say "similar to", not "similar with".

entry_json.definition: easy to do or understand, with nothing difficult in it
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The solution was simple once somebody explained it.
example_sentences: Follow these simple steps to register.
She prefers a simple life in a small town.

entry_json.definition: from a time in the past until now
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I have lived in this city since 2018.
example_sentences: She has not eaten since breakfast.
Prices have risen steadily since the pandemic.

confusables.difference: Since gives the starting point: since Monday, since I was ten. For gives the length of time: for three days, for ten years. "I have worked here since 2020" equals "for five years".

entry_json.avoid: Since normally goes with the present perfect: "I have studied here since March", not "I study here since March".

entry_json.definition: to make music with your voice
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I sing in a choir on Wednesday evenings.
example_sentences: She sang two songs at the wedding.
The children sang together at the end of the term.

entry_json.definition: a person who sings, especially as a job
entry_json.own_context_sentence: My favourite singer is coming to the city in May.
example_sentences: She is a well-known singer in my country.
The singer thanked the audience and left the stage.

entry_json.definition: the activity of making music with your voice
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Singing in a group made my pronunciation much better.
example_sentences: She has taken singing lessons since she was six.
We could hear singing from the church.

entry_json.definition: only one; also not married
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Not a single student failed the exam this year.
example_sentences: I bought a single ticket rather than a return.
She is single and lives on her own.

entry_json.definition: a polite way of speaking to a man whose name you do not know
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The waiter said, "Your table is ready, sir."
example_sentences: Excuse me, sir, you dropped your ticket.
Formal letters can begin "Dear Sir or Madam".
entry_json.avoid: Sir is formal and used with strangers or customers. Do not use it with friends or classmates.

entry_json.definition: a girl or woman who has the same parents as you
entry_json.own_context_sentence: My older sister works as a nurse in the capital.
example_sentences: I have one sister and two brothers.
She is very close to her younger sister.

entry_json.definition: to put your body on a seat or on the ground, resting your weight there
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I sit at a desk for eight hours a day, which is bad for my back.
example_sentences: Please sit down and wait for your name to be called.
We sat by the window and watched the rain.

entry_json.definition: a place where something is or where something happens
entry_json.own_context_sentence: They are building a new hospital on the site of the old factory.
example_sentences: Visitors are not allowed on the building site.
The website was slow, so I tried another site.

confusables.difference: They sound the same. A site is a place; a sight is something you see, as in "the sights of London" or "lose your sight".

entry_json.definition: all the things that are happening at one time in one place
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The housing situation in my city has become very difficult.
example_sentences: The economic situation has improved slightly.
In that situation I would ask for help.

entry_json.definition: how big or small something is
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The size of the classes matters more than the size of the school.
example_sentences: What size shoes do you take?
The flat is a good size for two people.

entry_json.definition: to move over snow on long narrow pieces of wood or plastic
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I learned to ski on a school trip when I was fourteen.
example_sentences: They ski every winter in the mountains.
He broke his arm trying to ski down a steep slope.

entry_json.definition: the sport of moving over snow on skis
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Skiing is expensive, so I only go once every few years.
example_sentences: Skiing holidays are popular in January and February.
She took up skiing after moving to Switzerland.

entry_json.definition: the ability to do something well, learned through practice
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Listening is the skill I need to work on most.
example_sentences: Employers look for communication skills.
Cooking is a useful skill to have when you live alone.

entry_json.definition: the outside part that covers the body of a person or animal
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Strong sun damages your skin even on cloudy days.
example_sentences: Use cream if your skin is dry in winter.
The skin of the fruit can be eaten.

entry_json.definition: a piece of clothing for women that covers the body from the middle down over the legs
entry_json.own_context_sentence: She wore a long skirt and a plain jacket to the interview.
example_sentences: The uniform is a grey skirt and a white shirt.
This skirt is too short for the office.

entry_json.definition: the space above the earth where you see clouds and the sun
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The sky was completely clear the morning we arrived.
example_sentences: Dark clouds filled the sky before the storm.
City lights make it hard to see stars in the night sky.

entry_json.definition: to rest with your eyes closed and your mind not active
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I sleep badly the night before an exam.
example_sentences: He slept for ten hours after the flight.
Most adults need seven or eight hours of sleep.

entry_json.definition: not moving or happening quickly
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The internet in my building is painfully slow in the evening.
example_sentences: Progress has been slow but steady.
The traffic was slow because of the roadworks.

entry_json.definition: in a way that is not quick
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Speak slowly and the examiner will follow you easily.
example_sentences: The number of cars is slowly falling in the city centre.
She read the question slowly and then answered.

entry_json.definition: not big in size or amount
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I grew up in a small town with one school and one shop.
example_sentences: There was only a small difference between the two groups.
A small flat in the centre costs more than a house outside.

confusables.difference: Small is the neutral word for size. Little often carries feeling, such as affection or dislike, and usually comes before a noun: "a lovely little garden".

entry_json.definition: a mobile phone that can also go online and run programs
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Almost every student in my class does their reading on a smartphone.
example_sentences: He checks his smartphone the moment he wakes up.
Smartphones have replaced cameras for most people.

entry_json.definition: to notice something with your nose
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I could smell fresh bread from the bakery downstairs.
example_sentences: The kitchen smells wonderful.
Something in the fridge smells bad.
entry_json.avoid: After smell use an adjective, not an adverb: "it smells nice", not "it smells nicely".

entry_json.definition: to turn the corners of your mouth up to show you are happy or friendly
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The examiner smiled and asked me to sit down.
example_sentences: She smiled at me across the room.
He smiled when he heard the results.

entry_json.definition: the grey or black gas that rises from something burning
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Smoke from the traffic hangs over the city on still days.
example_sentences: Thick smoke was coming from the roof.
Smoke from wood fires damages people's lungs.

entry_json.definition: the habit of breathing in smoke from cigarettes
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Smoking has fallen sharply since the ban in public places.
example_sentences: Smoking is not allowed anywhere in the building.
He gave up smoking after his father became ill.

entry_json.definition: a long thin animal with no legs
entry_json.own_context_sentence: There are no dangerous snakes in the area where I grew up.
example_sentences: She is frightened of snakes.
The snake moved slowly across the path.

entry_json.definition: soft white pieces of ice that fall from the sky in cold weather
entry_json.own_context_sentence: We get heavy snow for about two weeks every January.
example_sentences: The snow closed the schools for three days.
There was still snow on the mountains in May.
entry_json.avoid: Snow is uncountable. Say "a lot of snow", never "many snows".

entry_json.definition: for that reason; also used before an adjective to mean very
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The train was cancelled, so I took a taxi.
example_sentences: It was so cold that the lake froze.
She was ill, so she stayed at home.

confusables.difference: So goes before an adjective on its own: "so cold". Such goes before a noun phrase: "such a cold day". Never "so a cold day".

entry_json.definition: something you use with water to make your hands or body clean
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Washing your hands with soap is the cheapest way to stop illness spreading.
example_sentences: There was no soap in the bathroom.
She bought a bar of soap and a towel.

entry_json.definition: the game of football, played by two teams of eleven players
entry_json.own_context_sentence: In my country soccer is watched by more people than any other sport.
example_sentences: He played soccer at university.
Soccer is the American word for what the British call football.

confusables.difference: They are the same game. Football is normal in British English; soccer is the American word. In an IELTS test with British examiners, football is safer.

entry_json.definition: connected with people and how they live together
entry_json.own_context_sentence: Social media has changed how young people spend their evenings.
example_sentences: The report looks at the social effects of long working hours.
She has a busy social life outside work.

entry_json.definition: all the people who live in a country, thought of as one group
entry_json.own_context_sentence: An ageing society will need many more nurses and carers.
example_sentences: Education benefits society as a whole.
In modern society people move house far more often.
entry_json.avoid: When you mean people in general, use society with no article: "Society is changing", not "The society is changing".

entry_json.definition: a soft piece of clothing you wear on your foot inside a shoe
entry_json.own_context_sentence: I keep a spare pair of socks in my bag in winter.
example_sentences: He was wearing odd socks.
These wool socks are warm enough for the mountains.

entry_json.definition: not hard when you touch it; also quiet and not loud
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The seats were soft enough to sleep on during the night bus.
example_sentences: She spoke in a soft voice so as not to wake the baby.
This bread is still soft after two days.

entry_json.definition: a member of an army
entry_json.own_context_sentence: My grandfather was a soldier for twenty years.
example_sentences: Soldiers were sent to help after the floods.
He trained as a soldier before becoming an engineer.

entry_json.definition: a way of solving a problem
entry_json.own_context_sentence: The simplest solution is to improve public transport.
